To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-4R signalling on DC’s is essential for the development of protective immunity in L. major infection.
DCs deficient for IL- 4Rα signalling are hypersusceptible to L. major and show reduced parasite killing functions and increased migratory capacity.
DCs play an essential role in the development of Th1 responses and that the early IL-4/IL-13 response on DCs is required for the generation of protective Th1 responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of DCs in the initiation of the immune response to L. major in the absence of IL-4R signalling.
understanding the role of IL-4 in DC priming and how it can be manipulated to induce Th1 responses in the BALB/c mouse.
elucidating the role of IL-4/IL-4R signalling in the early phase of infection and its role in DC mediated immune responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-4R signalling on DCs is required for the induction of protective immunity to L. major in BALB/c hosts.
IL-4R signalling on DCs is a major factor in determining susceptibility to cutaneous leishmaniasis.
IL-4R signalling in DC’s is essential to induce a protective Th1 response in BALB/c.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DCs are major etiological factors for disease susceptibility and dissemination, and their response to early IL-4/IL-13 signalling is critical to the outcome of the infection.
IL-4R signalling on DCs in the early stages of infection, is critical in the establishment of protective Th1 immunity in BALB/c and C57BL/10 mice.
DCs in the absence of IL-4R signaling are not capable of producing IL-12 and are unable to prime Th1 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early IL-4 mediated response in DCs is essential in the induction of protective immunity against L. major infection.
the IL-4R signalling in DCs is critical in the induction of Th1 responses in susceptible mice and the development of protective immunity against L. major infection.
DCs are the primary target of early IL-12 production in the absence of IL-4R signalling.
